queries.prompt: Analyze these VPC Flow Log records showing `ACCEPT` inbound and `REJECT` outbound on `eni-0abc` to determine whether a Security Group or Network ACL blocked the traffic.
Inspect this `tshark` TCP packet capture summary showing `tcp.analysis.retransmission` on 4000-byte TLS packets with `MSS=8961` and diagnose the root cause.
Write a scoped CloudWatch Logs Insights query for our custom v5 VPC Flow Logs using `pkt-srcaddr` and `tcp-flags` to find the real EKS pod IP behind rejected flows.
Small `ping` and SSH sessions work across our Transit Gateway VPN, but large HTTPS POST uploads hang indefinitely and never finish the TLS handshake.
Connections through our Network Load Balancer work fine when active, but after sitting idle for 6 minutes the very next request gets a `TCP RST` (`Connection reset by peer`).

I captured a 300 MB `.pcapng` file on an EC2 host where file transfers crawl at 1.5 MB/s with zero packet loss—how do I export safe header-only CSV data for analysis and what causes zero-loss slowness?
Flow log line `5 123456789012 eni-011 10.0.1.8 10.0.2.9 44120 443 6 4 240 1731910000 1731910060 REJECT OK` has `reject-reason` `BPA` on one subnet and `SKIPDATA` on another—interpret both.
`tcpdump` on `i-09911` shows `SYN` -> `SYN-ACK` in `14ms`, `SYN-ACK` -> `ACK` in `0.04ms`, followed by `tcp.analysis.zero_window` from the peer. Fix the capture point and bottleneck.
Why are zero packets to `169.254.169.253` showing up in our `TrafficType=ALL` VPC Flow Logs on `eni-0abc123`?
Our EC2 instances in `ap-south-1` get `NXDOMAIN` for `orders.internal.corp` even though the Route 53 Private Hosted Zone is attached to the VPC—diagnose the DNS precedence collision.
Categorize our NAT Gateway traffic in GB and % across local S3, cross-region S3, and customer Elastic IPs to see why our NAT Gateway volume spiked.
Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch Network Flow Monitor agent (`aws-network-flow-monitor-agent`) on our Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instances.
